definition: An equation $\boldsymbol{r} = \boldsymbol{a} + \lambda\boldsymbol{b}$, $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$, where $\boldsymbol{a}$ is the position vector of one point on the line and $\boldsymbol{b}$ is a direction vector of the line, so each value of $\lambda$ gives the position vector $\boldsymbol{r}$ of one point on it.
A non-zero vector parallel to a line; any non-zero multiple of it is also a direction vector of that line.

A line written as one equation per coordinate in terms of a parameter $\lambda$, such as $x = x_0 + \lambda l$, $y = y_0 + \lambda m$, $z = z_0 + \lambda n$, where $(x_0, y_0, z_0)$ is a point on the line and $\begin{pmatrix}l\\m\\n\end{pmatrix}$ is a direction vector; each value of $\lambda$ gives one point.
